ruby "3.3.6"

# Bundle edge Rails instead: gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"
gem "rails", "7.0.8.7"
gem "concurrent-ruby", "1.3.4"

# The original asset pipeline for Rails [https://github.com/rails/sprockets-rails]
gem "sprockets-rails"

# Use postgresql as the database for Active Record
gem "pg", "1.6.0"

# Use the Puma web server [https://github.com/puma/puma]
gem "puma", "~> 5.0"

# Use JavaScript with ESM import maps [https://github.com/rails/importmap-rails]
gem "importmap-rails"

# Hotwire's SPA-like page accelerator [https://turbo.hotwired.dev]
gem "turbo-rails"

# Hotwire's modest JavaScript framework [https://stimulus.hotwired.dev]
gem "stimulus-rails"

# Build JSON APIs with ease [https://github.com/rails/jbuilder]
gem "jbuilder"

# Paginate the note list [https://github.com/ddnexus/pagy]
gem "pagy", "8.6.3"

# Run Active Job on Redis through Sidekiq [https://github.com/sidekiq/sidekiq]
gem "sidekiq", "6.5.12"
gem "redis", "4.8.1"

# Request citation metadata over HTTP [https://github.com/lostisland/faraday]
gem "faraday", "1.10.4"

# Use Kredis to get higher-level data types in Redis [https://github.com/rails/kredis]
# gem "kredis"

# Use Active Model has_secure_password [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_model_basics.html#securepassword]
gem "bcrypt", "~> 3.1.7"

# Windows does not include zoneinfo files, so bundle the tzinfo-data gem
gem "tzinfo-data", platforms: %i[ mingw mswin x64_mingw jruby ]

# Reduces boot times through caching; required in config/boot.rb
gem "bootsnap", require: false

# Use Sass to process CSS
# gem "sassc-rails"

# Use Active Storage variants [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_storage_overview.html#transforming-images]
# gem "image_processing", "~> 1.2"

group :development, :test do
  # See https://guides.rubyonrails.org/debugging_rails_applications.html#debugging-with-the-debug-gem
  gem "debug", platforms: %i[ mri mingw x64_mingw ]
end

group :development do
  # Use console on exceptions pages [https://github.com/rails/web-console]
  gem "web-console"

  # Add speed badges [https://github.com/MiniProfiler/rack-mini-profiler]
  # gem "rack-mini-profiler"

  # Speed up commands on slow machines / big apps [https://github.com/rails/spring]
  # gem "spring"
end

group :test do
  # Use system testing [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/testing.html#system-testing]
  gem "capybara"
  gem "selenium-webdriver"

  # Rails 7.0's test runner is incompatible with Minitest 6
  gem "minitest", "~> 5.25"
end

     1	# A work identified by its DOI, shared by every reader who cites it. Readers'
     2	# own annotations stay on their notes. Its metadata, and the state of the latest
     3	# request for it, are shared too.
     4	class Citation < ApplicationRecord
     5	  has_many :notes, foreign_key: :citation_doi
     6	
     7	  enum :enrichment_status, { pending: 0, completed: 1, failed: 2 }, prefix: :enrichment
     8	
     9	  validates :doi, format: { with: %r{\A10\.\d{4,9}/\S+\z} }
    10	
    11	  # Marks the citation pending and queues a metadata lookup, unless one is
    12	  # already pending. Returns whether a lookup was queued. The job is queued under
    13	  # the row lock, so a failed enqueue rolls back the pending state.
    14	  def request_enrichment
    15	    with_lock do
    16	      if enrichment_pending?
    17	        false
    18	      else
    19	        update!(enrichment_status: :pending, enrichment_error: nil)
    20	        CitationEnrichmentJob.perform_later(self)
    21	        true
    22	      end
    23	    end
    24	  end
    25	
    26	  # Asks the provider for this DOI's metadata. A permanent refusal marks the
    27	  # enrichment failed; an unavailable provider raises so the job can retry.
    28	  def enrich
    29	    metadata = Provider.new.lookup(doi)
    30	    record_enrichment(title: metadata.title, source_url: metadata.source_url, enrichment_status: :completed, enrichment_error: nil)
    31	  rescue Provider::Error => error
    32	    fail_enrichment(error.message)
    33	  end
    34	
    35	  def fail_enrichment(reason)
    36	    record_enrichment(enrichment_status: :failed, enrichment_error: reason)
    37	  end
    38	
    39	  private
    40	    # The job can load this citation before the request that queued it commits.
    41	    # Taking the row lock waits for that commit and reloads, so the result is
    42	    # written even when it equals the values loaded earlier.
    43	    def record_enrichment(attributes)
    44	      with_lock { update!(attributes) }
    45	    end
    46	end

     1	# A Markdown file of one notebook's notes, written by ExportJob. The reader can
     2	# cancel it while it is queued or working; the worker checks between notes and
     3	# stops. A completed file can be downloaded until it expires.
     4	class Export < ApplicationRecord
     5	  AVAILABLE_FOR = 24.hours
     6	
     7	  belongs_to :notebook
     8	  has_one_attached :file
     9	
    10	  enum :status, { queued: 0, working: 1, completed: 2, cancelled: 3 }
    11	
    12	  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
    13	
    14	  def cancellable?
    15	    queued? || working?
    16	  end
    17	
    18	  # Cancels a queued or working export. Returns whether it was cancelled.
    19	  def cancel
    20	    with_lock do
    21	      if cancellable?
    22	        update!(status: :cancelled)
    23	      else
    24	        false
    25	      end
    26	    end
    27	  end
    28	
    29	  # Writes the notebook's notes, oldest first, under its export heading. Progress
    30	  # is saved after each note. A cancelled export stops before the next note and
    31	  # keeps no file.
    32	  def generate
    33	    notes = notebook.notes.with_rich_text_body.order(:created_at, :id).to_a
    34	    return unless start(notes.size)
    35	
    36	    fragments = ["# #{notebook.export_heading || notebook.name}\n"]
    37	    notes.each_with_index do |note, index|
    38	      fragments << markdown_for(note)
    39	      return unless record_progress(index + 1)
    40	    end
    41	
    42	    finish(fragments.sum)
    43	  end
    44	
    45	  # The authoritative check for downloading the file.
    46	  def downloadable?
    47	    completed? && expires_at.future?
    48	  end
    49	
    50	  private
    51	    # A retried job starts again from the first note.
    52	    def start(total)
    53	      with_lock do
    54	        update!(status: :working, processed_notes_count: 0, total_notes_count: total) if cancellable?
    55	      end
    56	    end
    57	
    58	    def record_progress(count)
    59	      with_lock do
    60	        update!(processed_notes_count: count) unless cancelled?
    61	      end
    62	    end
    63	
    64	    # The file is stored before the export is marked completed, so a completed
    65	    # export always has one.
    66	    def finish(markdown)
    67	      blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(io: StringIO.new(markdown),
    68	        filename: "#{notebook.slug}.md", content_type: "text/markdown")
    69	
    70	      completed = with_lock do
    71	        update!(file: blob, status: :completed, expires_at: AVAILABLE_FOR.from_now) unless cancelled?
    72	      end
    73	
    74	      blob.purge unless completed
    75	    end
    76	
    77	    def markdown_for(note)
    78	      body = note.body.to_plain_text.strip
    79	      markdown = "\n## #{note.title.squish}\n"
    80	      markdown += "\n#{body}\n" if body.present?
    81	      markdown
    82	    end
    83	end

     1	require "csv"
     2	
     3	# A CSV of notes for one notebook. A preview reads and validates the rows without
     4	# saving anything. Applying validates them again and saves the import with every
     5	# row's note, or saves nothing.
     6	class Import < ApplicationRecord
     7	  HEADERS = %w[ title body_html doi annotation reminder_epoch ]
     8	  MAXIMUM_SIZE = 100.kilobytes
     9	  MAXIMUM_ROWS = 100
    10	
    11	  Row = Struct.new(:line, :note, :annotation)
    12	
    13	  belongs_to :notebook
    14	  has_many :notes, dependent: :nullify
    15	
    16	  validate :csv_is_importable, on: :create
    17	
    18	  # Reads one byte past the limit, which is enough to reject a larger file.
    19	  def file=(upload)
    20	    self.csv = String.new(upload.read(MAXIMUM_SIZE + 1).to_s, encoding: Encoding::UTF_8)
    21	  end
    22	
    23	  def csv
    24	    @csv.to_s
    25	  end
    26	
    27	  def csv=(text)
    28	    @csv = text.to_s
    29	    @rows = nil
    30	  end
    31	
    32	  def rows
    33	    parse unless @rows
    34	    @rows
    35	  end
    36	
    37	  # The reader's annotations by source line.
    38	  def annotations
    39	    rows.each_with_object(ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess.new) do |row, annotations|
    40	      annotations[row.line] = row.annotation
    41	    end
    42	  end
    43	
    44	  # Validates the file and every row without saving. Returns whether the import
    45	  # can be applied, leaving the errors on the import and each row's note.
    46	  def preview
    47	    valid? && rows.map { |row| row.note.valid? }.all?
    48	  end
    49	
    50	  def apply
    51	    return false if invalid?
    52	
    53	    transaction do
    54	      save!
    55	      rows.each do |row|
    56	        return false unless row.note.save
    57	      end
    58	    end
    59	
    60	    true
    61	  end
    62	
    63	  def receipt
    64	    CSV.generate do |csv|
    65	      csv << %w[ title doi ]
    66	      notes.includes(:citation).order(:id).each do |note|
    67	        citation = note.citation
    68	        csv << [ note.title, citation && citation[:id] ]
    69	      end
    70	    end
    71	  end
    72	
    73	  private
    74	    def parse
    75	      @rows, @headers, @problem = [], nil, nil
    76	      return if csv.bytesize > MAXIMUM_SIZE || !csv.valid_encoding?
    77	
    78	      reader = CSV.new(csv.delete_prefix("\uFEFF").encode(universal_newline: true))
    79	      citations = {}
    80	      next_line = 1
    81	
    82	      reader.each do |fields|
    83	        line, next_line = next_line, next_line + reader.line.count("\n")
    84	
    85	        if @headers.nil?
    86	          @headers = fields.map { |field| field.to_s.strip }
    87	          break if @headers != HEADERS
    88	        elsif fields.size != HEADERS.size && fields.any?
    89	          @problem = "line #{line} has #{fields.size} fields instead of #{HEADERS.size}"
    90	          break
    91	        elsif fields.any?
    92	          @rows << build_row(line, fields, citations)
    93	          break if @rows.size > MAXIMUM_ROWS
    94	        end
    95	      end
    96	    rescue CSV::MalformedCSVError => error
    97	      @problem = "it is not valid CSV (#{error.message})"
    98	    end
    99	
   100	    # Rows naming the same DOI share one citation, so it is created only once.
   101	    def build_row(line, fields, citations)
   102	      title, body_html, doi, annotation, reminder_epoch = fields.map { |field| field.to_s.strip }
   103	      citation = citations[doi] ||= Citation.find_or_initialize_by(doi: doi) if doi.present?
   104	
   105	      note = Note.new(notebook: notebook, import: self, title: title, body: body_html, citation: citation,
   106	        annotation: annotation.presence, reminder_epoch: reminder_epoch.presence)
   107	
   108	      Row.new(line, note, annotation.presence)
   109	    end
   110	
   111	    def csv_is_importable
   112	      rows
   113	
   114	      if csv.empty?
   115	        errors.add(:csv, :blank)
   116	      elsif csv.bytesize > MAXIMUM_SIZE
   117	        errors.add(:csv, "must be #{ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(MAXIMUM_SIZE)} or smaller")
   118	      elsif !csv.valid_encoding?
   119	        errors.add(:csv, "must be UTF-8 text")
   120	      elsif @problem
   121	        errors.add(:csv, "cannot be read because #{@problem}")
   122	      elsif @headers != HEADERS
   123	        errors.add(:csv, "must start with the header row #{HEADERS.join(",")}")
   124	      elsif rows.empty?
   125	        errors.add(:csv, "must contain at least one note")
   126	      elsif rows.size > MAXIMUM_ROWS
   127	        errors.add(:csv, "must contain #{MAXIMUM_ROWS} notes or fewer")
   128	      end
   129	    end
   130	end

    28	  # Cites the shared citation with this exact DOI, ignoring surrounding whitespace.
    29	  # A blank DOI removes the citation from the note.

    31	    doi = doi.to_s.strip

    35	  # The reminder time in the reader's time zone.
    36	  def reminder_at
    37	    Time.find_zone!(notebook.user.time_zone).at(reminder_epoch) if reminder_epoch
    38	  end
    39	
    40	  # Twenty-four elapsed hours after the reminder time, for postponing it a day.
    41	  # The result keeps the reminder's UTC offset, so across a daylight saving
    42	  # change its wall-clock time differs from the reader's local time.
    43	  def next_day_reminder_at
    44	    reminder_at.to_time + 86_400
    45	  end
    46	
    47	  def reminder_scheduled?
    48	    reminder_job_id.present? && reminder_sent_at.nil?
    49	  end
    50	
    51	  # Schedules an email reminder at the given time in seconds since 1970, by
    52	  # default the stored one, such as an imported reminder. It replaces any
    53	  # earlier reminder for this note: the earlier job sends nothing when it runs.
    54	  # Returns whether the reminder was scheduled. The job is queued under the row
    55	  # lock, so a failed enqueue leaves the previous reminder in place.
    56	  def schedule_reminder(epoch = reminder_epoch)
    57	    with_lock do
    58	      self.reminder_epoch = epoch
    59	
    60	      if reminder_epoch && valid?
    61	        job = NoteReminderJob.set(wait_until: reminder_epoch).perform_later(self)
    62	        update!(reminder_job_id: job.job_id, reminder_sent_at: nil)
    63	      else
    64	        errors.add(:base, "Choose a date and time for the reminder") if reminder_epoch.nil?
    65	        restore_attributes([:reminder_epoch])
    66	        false
    67	      end
    68	    end
    69	  end
    70	
    71	  def postpone_reminder
    72	    reminder_scheduled? && schedule_reminder(next_day_reminder_at.to_i)
    73	  end
    74	
    75	  # Sends the reminder if the given job is still the one scheduled for it.
    76	  # Taking the row lock waits for the request that queued the job to commit.
    77	  def send_reminder(job_id)
    78	    with_lock do
    79	      if reminder_job_id == job_id && reminder_scheduled?
    80	        update!(reminder_sent_at: Time.current)
    81	        ReminderMailer.with(note: self).note_reminder.deliver_now
    82	      end
    83	    end
    84	  end
    85

    91	    self.tags = list.to_s.split(",").map(&:strip).reject(&:blank?).uniq

    97	        errors.add(:body, "attachments must be #{ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(MAXIMUM_ATTACHMENT_SIZE)} or smaller")
    98	      end
    99	    end

     1	class User < ApplicationRecord
     2	  # Keep digest reservations past the end of their UTC day.
     3	  DIGEST_RESERVATIONS_KEPT_FOR = 2.days
     4	
     5	  has_secure_password
     6	
     7	  has_many :notebooks, dependent: :destroy
     8	  has_many :notes, through: :notebooks
     9	
    10	  before_validation { self.email = email.to_s.strip.downcase }
    11	
    12	  validates :email, presence: true, uniqueness: true
    13	  validates :time_zone, inclusion: { in: ActiveSupport::TimeZone.all.map(&:name) }
    14	
    15	  def self.authenticate(email, password)
    16	    find_by(email: email.to_s.strip.downcase)&.authenticate(password)
    17	  end
    18	
    19	  # Reads a date and time the reader entered, such as "2026-10-31T09:00", in
    20	  # their time zone. Returns nil when it is blank or not a valid time.
    21	  def local_time(text)
    22	    Time.find_zone!(time_zone).iso8601(text.to_s) if text.present?
    23	  rescue ArgumentError
    24	    nil
    25	  end
    26	
    27	  # Queues an email digest of ready notes updated today (UTC), unless the reader
    28	  # has already requested one for that UTC day. Returns whether a digest was queued.
    29	  #
    30	  # A Redis set of reader IDs for each day holds the reservations. If the job
    31	  # cannot be queued, the reservation is released and the error raised, so the
    32	  # reader can ask again. This prevents repeated requests, not repeated
    33	  # deliveries: a job that Sidekiq retries can send its digest more than once.
    34	  def request_digest
    35	    requested_at = Time.current.in_time_zone(time_zone)
    36	    key = "digest_requests:#{requested_at.utc.to_date.iso8601}"
    37	
    38	    if Sidekiq.redis { |redis| redis.sadd(key, id) }
    39	      begin
    40	        Sidekiq.redis { |redis| redis.expire(key, DIGEST_RESERVATIONS_KEPT_FOR.to_i) }
    41	        DigestJob.perform_later(self, requested_at, reading_completion)
    42	      rescue StandardError
    43	        Sidekiq.redis { |redis| redis.srem(key, id) }
    44	        raise
    45	      end
    46	
    47	      true
    48	    else
    49	      false
    50	    end
    51	  end
    52	
    53	  # The share of the reader's notes that are ready, from 0 to 1.
    54	  def reading_completion
    55	    total = notes.count
    56	    total.zero? ? BigDecimal("0") : (BigDecimal(notes.status_ready.count) / total).round(4)
    57	  end
    58	end

     1	# The configured citation metadata service. It answers GET /works?doi=... with a
     2	# JSON title and source URL, using HTTP basic authentication. Settings come from
     3	# config/secrets.yml, which reads them from the environment.
     4	class Citation::Provider
     5	  # The provider answered, but cannot supply metadata for this DOI.
     6	  class Error < StandardError; end
     7	
     8	  # The provider cannot answer now. Asking again later may succeed.
     9	  class Unavailable < StandardError; end
    10	
    11	  Metadata = Struct.new(:title, :source_url)
    12	
    13	  def initialize(settings = Rails.application.secrets.citation_provider.to_h)
    14	    @url, @user, @password = settings.values_at(:url, :user, :password)
    15	  end
    16	
    17	  def lookup(doi)
    18	    raise Error, "No citation provider is configured" if @url.blank?
    19	
    20	    response = connection.get("works", doi: doi)
    21	
    22	    case response.status
    23	    when 200 then metadata_from(response.body)
    24	    when 401, 403 then raise Error, "The provider rejected the configured credentials (HTTP #{response.status})"
    25	    when 404 then raise Error, "The provider has no record of this DOI"
    26	    when 429, 500..599 then raise Unavailable, "The provider is unavailable (HTTP #{response.status})"
    27	    else raise Error, "The provider gave an unexpected response (HTTP #{response.status})"
    28	    end
    29	  rescue Faraday::ConnectionFailed, Faraday::TimeoutError => error
    30	    raise Unavailable, "The provider could not be reached (#{error.message})"
    31	  end
    32	
    33	  private
    34	    # Retries a GET once on 503 before reporting the provider unavailable.
    35	    def connection
    36	      Faraday.new(url: @url, request: { open_timeout: 2, timeout: 5 }) do |faraday|
    37	        faraday.request :retry, max: 1, retry_statuses: [503]
    38	        faraday.request :basic_auth, @user, @password
    39	      end
    40	    end
    41	
    42	    def metadata_from(body)
    43	      attributes = JSON.parse(body)
    44	      title, source_url = attributes["title"], attributes["url"] if attributes.is_a?(Hash)
    45	
    46	      if title.is_a?(String) && title.present? && web_url?(source_url)
    47	        Metadata.new(title.strip, source_url)
    48	      else
    49	        raise Error, "The provider's response did not include a title and web address"
    50	      end
    51	    rescue JSON::ParserError
    52	      raise Error, "The provider's response was not valid JSON"
    53	    end
    54	
    55	    def web_url?(url)
    56	      uri = URI.parse(url.to_s)
    57	      uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) && uri.host.present?
    58	    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
    59	      false
    60	    end
    61	end

     1	# A native Sidekiq job, so its job ID can be shown with the export. Sidekiq
     2	# stores arguments as JSON, so the options arrive with string keys.
     3	class ExportJob
     4	  include Sidekiq::Job

# Architecture

## Starting point

Margin Notes is a reading-notebook application. Implemented so far:

- A reader (`User`) signs in with email and password through `has_secure_password`.
  `SessionsController` stores only the user ID in the Rails session.
  `ApplicationController#require_sign_in` protects the application's other
  controllers, but not Rails' Active Storage controllers.
- A reader owns `Notebook`s, and each `Note` belongs to one notebook. A note's
  owner is its notebook's owner, so `User#notes` (through notebooks) is the
  authorized note scope. There is no separate `user_id` on notes.
- `NotesController#index` serves `/notes` and its `/journal` alias. It lists the
  reader's notes newest first with an ID tie-breaker, and supports title search
  and notebook and status filters. `show` renders one note's rich body.
- Pagy 8.6.3 paginates that filtered list after ordering, 10 notes per page by
  default. The search form offers 5, 10, 25, or 50 as the `per_page` URL
  parameter. Larger requested sizes are capped at 50. Next and previous links keep
  the filters and page size. A blank, zero, negative, or nonnumeric page shows the
  first page, and a page past the end shows the last page. The form never sends
  an invalid size. A blank, zero, negative, or nonnumeric `per_page` in a URL is
  not handled, and Pagy raises `Pagy::VariableError`.
- A note's body is Action Text (`has_rich_text :body`), edited with Trix.
  Attachments are Active Storage blobs on the local Disk service. `Note` rejects
  saves that embed a blob over 1 MB. Direct uploads store blobs before this
  validation, without a size limit. Rejected or abandoned uploads remain
  unattached, and nothing purges them. No image processor is installed, so images
  use the original blobs, not variants. A migration converted existing plain-text
  bodies to escaped rich text.
- Action Text sanitizes rich text when it renders. The
  [Action Text initializer](config/initializers/action_text.rb) adds
  `details`/`summary` to the default allowlist for collapsible excerpts. Trix
  does not support those elements. Stored excerpts render as collapsible content,
  but saving them through the editor permanently flattens that structure, even
  when only tags or highlight change.
- Note tags are a JSON array in a text column, entered as a comma-separated
  list (`Note#tag_list`). The highlight color is `color` in the `settings` jsonb
  column, which the form edits as `highlight_color`.
- `NotebooksController#edit`/`update` are notebook settings. The slug is derived
  from the name on creation and is read-only afterward (`attr_readonly`). The
  settings form resubmits it unchanged. The export heading is stored in the
  serialized `preferences` hash. Markdown exports use both.
- A reader imports a CSV into one owned notebook. `ImportPreviewsController`
  reads the upload and renders a preview without saving. The preview page sends
  the CSV text back in a hidden field, and `ImportsController#create` reads and
  validates it again rather than trusting the preview. `Import#apply` saves the
  import and each row's note in one transaction. If any row cannot be saved,
  nothing from the batch remains. The receipt page and its CSV download list
  each imported note's title and DOI. Submitting the same preview twice creates
  two imports.
- `Import` accepts one format: UTF-8 CSV with the header row
  `title,body_html,doi,annotation,reminder_epoch`, at most 100 notes and 100 KB.
  Only the title is required. Previews identify rows by their source line, so a
  quoted multi-line body keeps the line where its row starts. Body HTML takes the
  same Action Text assignment and render-time sanitization as the editor.
- A `Citation` is identified by its DOI, the table's `doi` primary key, and is
  shared by every reader who cites it. A DOI is stored as given apart from
  surrounding whitespace, so case variants are different citations. Rows in one
  import share a new citation. Two simultaneous imports that introduce the same
  new DOI can conflict; the losing request fails with a server error and saves
  nothing. A reader's annotation and optional reminder epoch belong to the note,
  not the citation. Annotations are plain text in both the preview and note page;
  line breaks are preserved on the note page, but markup is displayed literally.
  Applying an import does not schedule its reminders; the reader schedules each
  one from its note.
- A reader can also enter a DOI on the note form (`Note#doi=`), which cites the
  shared citation with that exact, trimmed DOI or creates it.
- A reader requests metadata for the citation on one of their notes with
  `CitationEnrichmentsController#create`, nested under the note. It resolves the
  note through `current_user.notes`, so another reader's note, or a note without
  a DOI, is a 404. `Citation#request_enrichment` marks the citation pending and
  queues `CitationEnrichmentJob`, unless a request is already pending. The job
  calls `Citation#enrich`, which stores the provider's title and source URL and
  marks the citation completed, or records a failure message. Metadata and
  status belong to the shared citation, so every note citing the DOI shows them.
  The note page shows the state; it does not update itself while pending.
- `Citation::Provider` is the HTTP client for the metadata provider. It reads
  its URL and basic-auth credentials from [config/secrets.yml](config/secrets.yml)
  through `Rails.application.secrets`; that file reads them from the environment.
  Faraday retries a GET once on 503. A 401, 403, or 404, or a response without a
  title and an http(s) URL, fails the enrichment at once. A 429 or 5xx, timeout,
  or connection failure raises `Citation::Provider::Unavailable`. The job retries
  that with `retry_on`, three attempts in all at exponentially longer waits, then
  records the failure instead of passing the error to Sidekiq's own retries. A
  persistently unavailable provider therefore receives at most six requests per
  enrichment request. A job that fails for another reason uses Sidekiq's retries
  and leaves the citation pending meanwhile.
- [bin/citation-provider](bin/citation-provider) is a deterministic local stand-in
  for the provider, used for development and demonstrations. No real provider or
  credentials are configured.
- A reader exports an owned notebook as Markdown from its exports page
  (`ExportsController`, nested under the notebook). `Notebook#request_export`
  saves a queued `Export`, then queues the native Sidekiq job `ExportJob` and
  stores its job ID, which the page shows. The export is committed before the
  job is queued so the worker can always load it. If Redis refuses the job, the
  export is removed and the request fails. Each request creates a new export.
- `Export#generate`, run by the worker, marks the export working with the
  notebook's note count, then writes the notes oldest first (creation time, then
  ID). The file starts with the notebook's export heading, or its name when none
  is set. Each note is a second-level heading with its title on one line,
  followed by its body as Action Text plain text. Markdown characters are not
  escaped. Progress is saved after each note. A retried job starts again from
  the first note. There is no failed state: while Sidekiq retries a failing job,
  the export shows as working and the reader can cancel it.
- Cancelling (`ExportCancellationsController`) sets a queued or working export's
  persisted status to cancelled under its row lock. The worker checks that status
  before each note and before completing, then stops and keeps no file. Completed
  and cancelled exports cannot be cancelled.
- The worker uploads the file to Active Storage (`<slug>.md`) before marking the
  export completed, so a completed export always has a file. It can be downloaded
  for 24 hours (`Export::AVAILABLE_FOR`). `ExportDownloadsController` resolves the
  export through the reader's notebook, so another reader's export is a 404, and
  checks `Export#downloadable?` on every request before any conditional response.
  An expired, cancelled, or unfinished export redirects to the exports page. The
  file is sent by the application, never by an Active Storage URL, with an ETag
  and Last-Modified from the stored file and `private, must-revalidate`.
  A failed upload can leave an unattached blob row without a stored file. Nothing
  cleans up those rows, and each failed retry can leave another one.
- The exports page caches each completed export's availability indicator as a
  fragment that expires at the export's deadline. The download action does not
  read that cache. The page does not update itself while an export is queued or
  working. Nothing purges expired files; they remain in storage.
- A notebook's activity page (`ActivityReportsController#show`, nested under the
  notebook and linked from the notebooks list) shows how many of its notes were
  created on each UTC date, newest date first. It is read-only and resolves the
  notebook through `current_user.notebooks`, so another reader's notebook is a
  404. `Notebook#daily_note_counts` groups the notes by `DATE(created_at)` in
  PostgreSQL and reads the rows with a raw `select_rows`, which returns each date
  as ISO 8601 text; the method parses it with `Date.iso8601`. Every status counts,
  and dates without notes are omitted. The report is derived from the notes that
  exist when it is requested, not an activity log: deleting a note lowers its
  date's count, and nothing records past counts.
- Each reader has a time zone (`User#time_zone`, UTC by default), chosen on the
  account settings page (`AccountsController`). Reminder times use it. Digests
  follow UTC days, and other pages still show times in UTC.
- A note's reminder is its `reminder_epoch`, a time in seconds since 1970, set by
  an import or by the reader. `RemindersController#create`, nested under the
  note, reads a date and time the reader entered in their time zone
  (`User#local_time`), or, with none, uses the stored time. `Note#schedule_reminder`
  queues `NoteReminderJob` for that time with `set(wait_until:)` and stores the
  job's ID, under the note's row lock, so a failed enqueue keeps the earlier
  reminder. A local time that does not exist because of a daylight saving change
  moves forward, and an ambiguous one takes its first occurrence. A time in the
  past is sent as soon as a worker runs the job.
- Scheduling again, or postponing (`ReminderPostponementsController`), replaces the
  reminder. Earlier jobs stay in Sidekiq's schedule, but send nothing: when a job
  runs, `Note#send_reminder` takes the row lock and emails the reader only if its
  job ID is still the note's and the reminder has not been sent, then records
  `reminder_sent_at`. The note page shows whether a reminder is imported but not

require "sidekiq"

module ActiveJob
  module QueueAdapters
    # = Sidekiq adapter for Active Job
    #
    # Simple, efficient background processing for Ruby. Sidekiq uses threads to
    # handle many jobs at the same time in the same process. It does not
    # require \Rails but will integrate tightly with it to make background
    # processing dead simple.
    #
    # Read more about Sidekiq {here}[http://sidekiq.org].
    #
    # To use Sidekiq set the queue_adapter config to +:sidekiq+.
    #
    #   Rails.application.config.active_job.queue_adapter = :sidekiq
    class SidekiqAdapter < AbstractAdapter
      def initialize(*) # :nodoc:
        @stopping = false

        Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
          config.on(:quiet) { @stopping = true }
        end

        Sidekiq.configure_client do |config|
          config.on(:quiet) { @stopping = true }
        end
      end

      def check_adapter
        ActiveJob.deprecator.warn <<~MSG.squish
          The built-in `sidekiq` adapter is deprecated and will be removed in Rails 8.2.
          Please upgrade `sidekiq` gem to version 7.3.3 or later to use the `sidekiq` gem's adapter.
        MSG
      end

      def enqueue(job) # :nodoc:
        job.provider_job_id = JobWrapper.set(
          wrapped: job.class,
          queue: job.queue_name
        ).perform_async(job.serialize)
      end

      def enqueue_at(job, timestamp) # :nodoc:
        job.provider_job_id = JobWrapper.set(
          wrapped: job.class,
          queue: job.queue_name,
        ).perform_at(timestamp, job.serialize)
      end

      def enqueue_all(jobs) # :nodoc:
        enqueued_count = 0
        jobs.group_by(&:class).each do |job_class, same_class_jobs|
          same_class_jobs.group_by(&:queue_name).each do |queue, same_class_and_queue_jobs|
            immediate_jobs, scheduled_jobs = same_class_and_queue_jobs.partition { |job| job.scheduled_at.nil? }

            if immediate_jobs.any?
              jids = Sidekiq::Client.push_bulk(
                "class" => JobWrapper,
                "wrapped" => job_class,
                "queue" => queue,
                "args" => immediate_jobs.map { |job| [job.serialize] },
              )
              enqueued_count += jids.compact.size
            end

            if scheduled_jobs.any?
              jids = Sidekiq::Client.push_bulk(
                "class" => JobWrapper,
                "wrapped" => job_class,
                "queue" => queue,
                "args" => scheduled_jobs.map { |job| [job.serialize] },
                "at" => scheduled_jobs.map { |job| job.scheduled_at&.to_f }
              )
              enqueued_count += jids.compact.size
            end
          end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module ActiveJob
  # Provides behavior for enqueuing jobs.

  # Can be raised by adapters if they wish to communicate to the caller a reason
  # why the adapter was unexpectedly unable to enqueue a job.
  class EnqueueError < StandardError; end

  class << self
    # Push many jobs onto the queue at once without running enqueue callbacks.
    # Queue adapters may communicate the enqueue status of each job by setting
    # successfully_enqueued and/or enqueue_error on the passed-in job instances.
    def perform_all_later(*jobs)
      jobs.flatten!
      jobs.group_by(&:queue_adapter).each do |queue_adapter, adapter_jobs|
        instrument_enqueue_all(queue_adapter, adapter_jobs) do
          if queue_adapter.respond_to?(:enqueue_all)
            queue_adapter.enqueue_all(adapter_jobs)
          else
            adapter_jobs.each do |job|
              job.successfully_enqueued = false
              if job.scheduled_at
                queue_adapter.enqueue_at(job, job.scheduled_at.to_f)
              else
                queue_adapter.enqueue(job)
              end
              job.successfully_enqueued = true
            rescue EnqueueError => e
              job.enqueue_error = e
            end
            adapter_jobs.count(&:successfully_enqueued?)
          end
        end
      end
      nil
    end
  end

  module Enqueuing
    extend ActiveSupport::Concern

    included do
      ##
      # :singleton-method:
      #
      # Defines if enqueueing this job from inside an Active Record transaction
      # automatically defers the enqueue to after the transaction commits.
      #
      # It can be set on a per job basis:
      #  - true forces the job to be deferred.
      #  - false forces the job to be queued immediately.
      class_attribute :enqueue_after_transaction_commit, instance_accessor: false, instance_predicate: false, default: false
    end

    # Includes the +perform_later+ method for job initialization.
    module ClassMethods
      # Push a job onto the queue. By default the arguments must be either String,
      # Integer, Float, NilClass, TrueClass, FalseClass, BigDecimal, Symbol, Date,
      # Time, DateTime, ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone, ActiveSupport::Duration,
      # Hash, ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess, Array, Range, or
      # GlobalID::Identification instances, although this can be extended by adding
      # custom serializers.
      #
      # Returns an instance of the job class queued with arguments available in
      # Job#arguments or +false+ if the enqueue did not succeed.
      #
      # After the attempted enqueue, the job will be yielded to an optional block.
      #
      # If Active Job is used conjointly with Active Record, and #perform_later is called
      # inside an Active Record transaction, then the enqueue is implicitly deferred to after
      # the transaction is committed, or dropped if it's rolled back. In such case #perform_later
      # will return the job instance like if it was successfully enqueued, but will still return
      # +false+ if a callback prevented the job from being enqueued.
      #
      # This behavior can be changed on a per job basis:
      #
      #  class NotificationJob < ApplicationJob
      #    self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = false
      #  end
      def perform_later(...)
        job = job_or_instantiate(...)
        enqueue_result = job.enqueue

        yield job if block_given?

        enqueue_result
      end

      private
        def job_or_instantiate(*args, &) # :doc:
          args.first.is_a?(self) ? args.first : new(*args)
        end
        ruby2_keywords(:job_or_instantiate)
    end

    # Enqueues the job to be performed by the queue adapter.
    #
    # ==== Options
    # * <tt>:wait</tt> - Enqueues the job with the specified delay
    # * <tt>:wait_until</tt> - Enqueues the job at the time specified
    # * <tt>:queue</tt> - Enqueues the job on the specified queue
    # * <tt>:priority</tt> - Enqueues the job with the specified priority
    #
    # ==== Examples
    #
    #    my_job_instance.enqueue
    #    my_job_instance.enqueue wait: 5.minutes
    #    my_job_instance.enqueue queue: :important
    #    my_job_instance.enqueue wait_until: Date.tomorrow.midnight
    #    my_job_instance.enqueue priority: 10
    def enqueue(options = {})
      set(options)
      self.successfully_enqueued = false

      raw_enqueue

      if successfully_enqueued?
        self
      else
        false
      end
    end

    private
      def raw_enqueue
        run_callbacks :enqueue do
          _raw_enqueue
        end
      end

      def _raw_enqueue
        if scheduled_at
          queue_adapter.enqueue_at self, scheduled_at.to_f
        else
          queue_adapter.enqueue self
        end

        self.successfully_enqueued = true
      rescue EnqueueError => e
        self.enqueue_error = e
      end
  end
end

      # defaults for versions prior to the target version. See the
      # {configuration guide}[https://guides.rubyonrails.org/configuring.html#versioned-default-values]

      def load_defaults(target_version)

        # 1. Add an accessor on the target object (e.g. the ActiveJob class for

        #    applications.
        # 3. Implement the behavior change based on the config value.

        #    configure the default value.
        # 5. Add a commented out section in the `new_framework_defaults` to
        #    configure the default value again.

        # 1. Update or remove the entry in the guides.

      def encoding=(value)

      def paths

          paths = super

      # Load the database YAML without evaluating ERB. This allows us to
      # create the rake tasks for multiple databases without filling in the
      # configuration values or loading the environment. Do not use this
      # method.
      #
      # This uses a DummyERB custom compiler so YAML can ignore the ERB
      # tags and load the database.yml for the rake tasks.
      def load_database_yaml # :nodoc:
        if path = paths["config/database"].existent.first
          require "rails/application/dummy_erb_compiler"

          yaml = DummyERB.new(Pathname.new(path).read).result

          if YAML.respond_to?(:unsafe_load)
            YAML.unsafe_load(yaml) || {}
          else
            YAML.load(yaml) || {}
          end
        else
          {}
        end
      end

      # Loads and returns the entire raw configuration of database from
      # values stored in <tt>config/database.yml</tt>.
      def database_configuration
        path = paths["config/database"].existent.first
        yaml = Pathname.new(path) if path

        config = if yaml&.exist?
          loaded_yaml = ActiveSupport::ConfigurationFile.parse(yaml)
          if (shared = loaded_yaml.delete("shared"))
            loaded_yaml.each do |env, config|
              if config.is_a?(Hash) && config.values.all?(Hash)
                config.map do |name, sub_config|
                  sub_config.reverse_merge!(shared)
                end
              else
                config.reverse_merge!(shared)
              end
            end
          end
          Hash.new(shared).merge(loaded_yaml)
        elsif ENV["DATABASE_URL"]
          # Value from ENV['DATABASE_URL'] is set to default database connection
          # by Active Record.
          {}
        else
          raise "Could not load database configuration. No such file - #{paths["config/database"].instance_variable_get(:@paths)}"
        end

        config
      rescue => e
        raise e, "Cannot load database configuration:\n#{e.message}", e.backtrace
      end

      # the +ActionDispatch::Session+ namespace:

      #   config.session_store :my_custom_store
      def session_store(new_session_store = nil, **options)
        if new_session_store
          if new_session_store == :active_record_store

def within_new_transaction(isolation: nil, joinable: true)
        @connection.lock.synchronize do
          transaction = begin_transaction(isolation: isolation, joinable: joinable)
          ret = yield
          completed = true
          ret
        rescue Exception => error
          if transaction
            transaction.state.invalidate! if error.is_a? ActiveRecord::TransactionRollbackError
            rollback_transaction
            after_failure_actions(transaction, error)
          end

          raise
        ensure
          if transaction
            if error
              # @connection still holds an open or invalid transaction, so we must not
              # put it back in the pool for reuse.
              @connection.throw_away! unless transaction.state.rolledback?
            elsif Thread.current.status == "aborting" || (!completed && transaction.written)
              # The transaction is still open but the block returned earlier.
              #
              # The block could return early because of a timeout or because the thread is aborting,
              # so we are rolling back to make sure the timeout didn't caused the transaction to be
              # committed incompletely.
              rollback_transaction
            else
              begin
                commit_transaction
              rescue Exception
                rollback_transaction(transaction) unless transaction.state.completed?
                raise
              end
            end
          end
        end
      end

def serialize(attr_name, coder: nil, type: Object, comparable: false, yaml: {}, **options)
          coder ||= default_column_serializer
          unless coder
            raise ArgumentError, <<~MSG.squish
              missing keyword: :coder

              If no default coder is configured, a coder must be provided to `serialize`.
            MSG
          end

          column_serializer = build_column_serializer(attr_name, coder, type, yaml)

          attribute(attr_name, **options)

          decorate_attributes([attr_name]) do |attr_name, cast_type|
            if type_incompatible_with_serialize?(cast_type, coder, type)
              raise ColumnNotSerializableError.new(attr_name, cast_type)
            end

            cast_type = cast_type.subtype if Type::Serialized === cast_type
            Type::Serialized.new(cast_type, column_serializer, comparable: comparable)
          end
        end

def determine_delay(seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm:, executions:, jitter: JITTER_DEFAULT)
        jitter = jitter == JITTER_DEFAULT ? self.class.retry_jitter : (jitter || 0.0)

        case seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm
        when  :polynomially_longer
          # This delay uses a polynomial backoff strategy, which was previously misnamed as exponential
          delay = executions**4
          delay_jitter = determine_jitter_for_delay(delay, jitter)
          delay + delay_jitter + 2
        when ActiveSupport::Duration, Integer
          delay = seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm.to_i
          delay_jitter = determine_jitter_for_delay(delay, jitter)
          delay + delay_jitter
        when Proc
          algorithm = seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm
          algorithm.call(executions)
        else
          raise "Couldn't determine a delay based on #{seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm.inspect}"
        end
      def retry_on(*exceptions, wait: 3.seconds, attempts: 5, queue: nil, priority: nil, jitter: JITTER_DEFAULT, report: false)
        rescue_from(*exceptions) do |error|
          executions = executions_for(exceptions)
          if attempts == :unlimited || executions < attempts
            ActiveSupport.error_reporter.report(error, source: "application.active_job") if report
            retry_job wait: determine_delay(seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm: wait, executions: executions, jitter: jitter), queue: queue, priority: priority, error: error
          else
            if block_given?
              instrument :retry_stopped, error: error do
                yield self, error
              end
              run_after_discard_procs(error)
            else
              instrument :retry_stopped, error: error
              run_after_discard_procs(error)
              raise error
            end
          end
        end

    class TimeWithZoneSerializer < ObjectSerializer # :nodoc:

      def deserialize(hash)

      end

      if attachment.respond_to?(:model_name)

    end

    def sanitizer_allowed_attributes
      allowed_attributes || (sanitizer.class.allowed_attributes + ActionText::Attachment::ATTRIBUTES)
    end
  end

require "rails"
require "action_controller/railtie"
require "active_record/railtie"
require "active_storage/engine"

require "action_text"
require "action_text/trix"

module ActionText
  class Engine < Rails::Engine
    isolate_namespace ActionText
    config.eager_load_namespaces << ActionText

    config.action_text = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
    config.action_text.attachment_tag_name = "action-text-attachment"
    config.autoload_once_paths = %W(
      #{root}/app/helpers
      #{root}/app/models
    )

    initializer "action_text.deprecator", before: :load_environment_config do |app|
      app.deprecators[:action_text] = ActionText.deprecator
    end

    initializer "action_text.attribute" do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record) do
        include ActionText::Attribute
        prepend ActionText::Encryption
      end
    end

    initializer "action_text.asset" do
      if Rails.application.config.respond_to?(:assets)
        Rails.application.config.assets.precompile += %w( actiontext.js actiontext.esm.js )
      end
    end

    initializer "action_text.attachable" do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_storage_blob) do
        include ActionText::Attachable

        def previewable_attachable?
          representable?
        end

        def attachable_plain_text_representation(caption = nil)
          "[#{caption || filename}]"
        end

        def to_trix_content_attachment_partial_path
          nil
        end
      end
    end

    initializer "action_text.helper" do
      %i[action_controller_base action_mailer].each do |base|
        ActiveSupport.on_load(base) do
          helper ActionText::Engine.helpers
        end
      end
    end

    initializer "action_text.renderer" do
      %i[action_controller_base action_mailer].each do |base|
        ActiveSupport.on_load(base) do
          around_action do |controller, action|
            ActionText::Content.with_renderer(controller, &action)
          end
        end
      end
    end

    initializer "action_text.system_test_helper" do

          end
          [sql.freeze, binds, preparable]

def match(*path_or_actions, as: DEFAULT, via: nil, to: nil, controller: nil, action: nil, on: nil, defaults: nil, constraints: nil, anchor: nil, format: nil, path: nil, internal: nil, **mapping, &block)
          if path_or_actions.grep(Hash).any? && (deprecated_options = path_or_actions.extract_options!)
            as = assign_deprecated_option(deprecated_options, :as, :match) if deprecated_options.key?(:as)
            via ||= assign_deprecated_option(deprecated_options, :via, :match)
            to ||= assign_deprecated_option(deprecated_options, :to, :match)
            controller ||= assign_deprecated_option(deprecated_options, :controller, :match)
            action ||= assign_deprecated_option(deprecated_options, :action, :match)
            on ||= assign_deprecated_option(deprecated_options, :on, :match)
            defaults ||= assign_deprecated_option(deprecated_options, :defaults, :match)
            constraints ||= assign_deprecated_option(deprecated_options, :constraints, :match)
            anchor = assign_deprecated_option(deprecated_options, :anchor, :match) if deprecated_options.key?(:anchor)
            format = assign_deprecated_option(deprecated_options, :format, :match) if deprecated_options.key?(:format)
            path ||= assign_deprecated_option(deprecated_options, :path, :match)
            internal ||= assign_deprecated_option(deprecated_options, :internal, :match)
            assign_deprecated_options(deprecated_options, mapping, :match)
          end

          raise ArgumentError, "Wrong number of arguments (expect 1, got #{path_or_actions.count})" if path_or_actions.count > 1

          if path_or_actions.none? && mapping.any?
            hash_path, hash_to = mapping.find { |key, _| key.is_a?(String) }
            if hash_path.nil?
              raise ArgumentError, "Route path not specified"
            else
              mapping.delete(hash_path)
            end

            if hash_path
              path_or_actions.push hash_path
              case hash_to
              when Symbol
                action ||= hash_to
              when String
                if hash_to.include?("#")
                  to ||= hash_to
                else
                  controller ||= hash_to
                end
              else
                to ||= hash_to
              end
            end
          end

      # Returns string denoting the name of the configured queue adapter.
      # By default returns <tt>"async"</tt>.
      def queue_adapter_name
        self.queue_adapter = :async if _queue_adapter_name.nil?
        _queue_adapter_name
      end

      # Specify the backend queue provider. The default queue adapter
      # is the +:async+ queue. See QueueAdapters for more
      # information.
      def queue_adapter=(name_or_adapter)
        case name_or_adapter
        when Symbol, String
          queue_adapter = ActiveJob::QueueAdapters.lookup(name_or_adapter).new
          queue_adapter.try(:check_adapter)
          assign_adapter(name_or_adapter.to_s, queue_adapter)
        else
          if queue_adapter?(name_or_adapter)
            adapter_name = ActiveJob.adapter_name(name_or_adapter).underscore
            assign_adapter(adapter_name, name_or_adapter)
          else
            raise ArgumentError
          end
        end
      end

      private
        def assign_adapter(adapter_name, queue_adapter)
          self._queue_adapter_name = adapter_name
          self._queue_adapter = queue_adapter
        end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module ActiveJob
  module EnqueueAfterTransactionCommit # :nodoc:
    private
      def raw_enqueue
        if self.class.enqueue_after_transaction_commit
          self.successfully_enqueued = true
          ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit do
            self.successfully_enqueued = false
            super
          end
          self
        else
          super
        end
      end
  end
end
            @import.finalize
          end
      end
    end
    ```

    *Donal McBreen*

*   Defer invocation of ActiveJob enqueue callbacks until after commit when
    `enqueue_after_transaction_commit` is enabled.

    *Will Roever*

*   Add `report:` option to `ActiveJob::Base#retry_on` and `#discard_on`

    When the `report:` option is passed, errors will be reported to the error reporter
    before being retried / discarded.

    *Andrew Novoselac*

*   Accept a block for `ActiveJob::ConfiguredJob#perform_later`.

    This was inconsistent with a regular `ActiveJob::Base#perform_later`.

    *fatkodima*

content.content:
with `delete_all` which currently raises an error for unsupported statements.

    *Edouard Chin*

*   The table columns inside `schema.rb` are now sorted alphabetically.

    Previously they'd be sorted by creation order, which can cause merge conflicts when two
    branches modify the same table concurrently.

    *John Duff*

*   Introduce versions formatter for the schema dumper.

    It is now possible to override how schema dumper formats versions information inside the
    `structure.sql` file. Currently, the versions are simply sorted in the decreasing order.
    Within large teams, this can potentially cause many merge conflicts near the top of the list.

    Now, the custom formatter can be provided with a custom sorting logic (e.g. by hash values
    of the versions), which can greatly reduce the number of conflicts.

    *fatkodima*

*   Serialized attributes can now be marked as comparable.

    A not rare issue when working with serialized attributes is that the serialized representation of an object
    can change over time. Either because you are migrating from one serializer to the other (e.g. YAML to JSON or to msgpack),
    or because the serializer used subtly changed its output.

    One example is libyaml that used to have some extra trailing whitespaces, and recently fixed that.
    When this sorts of thing happen, you end up with lots of records that report being changed even though
    they aren't, which in the best case leads to a lot more writes to the database and in the worst case lead to nasty bugs.

    The solution is to instead compare the deserialized representation of the object, however Active Record
    can't assume the deserialized object has a working `==` method. Hence why this new functionality is opt-in.

    ```ruby
    serialize :config, type: Hash, coder: JSON, comparable: true
    ```

    *Jean Boussier*

    foreign key constraint violations.

*   Attributes filtered by `filter_attributes` will now also be filtered by `filter_parameters`
    so sensitive information is not leaked.

require "active_support/json"

module ActiveRecord
  module Coders # :nodoc:
    class JSON # :nodoc:
      DEFAULT_OPTIONS = { escape: false }.freeze

      def initialize(options = nil)
        @options = options ? DEFAULT_OPTIONS.merge(options) : DEFAULT_OPTIONS
        @encoder = ActiveSupport::JSON::Encoding.json_encoder.new(options)
      end

      def dump(obj)
        @encoder.encode(obj)
      end

      def load(json)
        ActiveSupport::JSON.decode(json, @options) unless json.blank?
      end
    end
  end

          def build_column_serializer(attr_name, coder, type, yaml = nil)
            # When ::JSON is used, force it to go through the Active Support JSON encoder
            # to ensure special objects (e.g. Active Record models) are dumped correctly
            # using the #as_json hook.

            if coder == ::JSON || coder == Coders::JSON
              coder = Coders::JSON.new
            end

            if coder == ::YAML || coder == Coders::YAMLColumn
              Coders::YAMLColumn.new(attr_name, type, **(yaml || {}))
            elsif coder.respond_to?(:new) && !coder.respond_to?(:load)
              coder.new(attr_name, type)
            elsif type && type != Object
              Coders::ColumnSerializer.new(attr_name, coder, type)
            else
              coder
            end
          end

def form_with(model: false, scope: nil, url: nil, format: nil, **options, &block)
        raise ArgumentError, "Passed nil to the :model argument, expect an object or false" if model.nil?

        options = { allow_method_names_outside_object: true, skip_default_ids: !form_with_generates_ids }.merge!(options)

        if model
          if url != false
            url ||= if format.nil?
              polymorphic_path(model, {})
            else
              polymorphic_path(model, format: format)
            end
          end

          model   = convert_to_model(_object_for_form_builder(model))
          scope ||= model_name_from_record_or_class(model).param_key
        end

        if block_given?
          builder = instantiate_builder(scope, model, options)
          output  = capture(builder, &block)
          options[:multipart] ||= builder.multipart?

          html_options = html_options_for_form_with(url, model, **options)
          form_tag_with_body(html_options, output)
        else
          html_options = html_options_for_form_with(url, model, **options)
          form_tag_html(html_options)
        end
      end

input.description: Inspect Integer type string coercion change

content.content:
*   Fix `ActiveModel::Type::BigInteger` truncating strings longer than 16 bytes when casting.

    `BigInteger` (and Active Record decimal columns without a scale) now limits
    the cast string to twice its `precision`, or to 2000 bytes when it has none.

    *Suliman Abdulrazzaq*

*   Limit the size of strings `ActiveModel::Type::Integer` will coerce with `to_i`.

    Calling `to_i` on very long strings can take a long time and could be used as
    a DoS vector. Integer casting now only considers the first `_limit * 4` bytes
    of a string (16 bytes for a default 4-byte integer, 32 bytes for an 8-byte
    bigint), which is enough to hold the maximum representable value plus a sign
    or a short slug suffix.

    *Aaron Patterson*, *Jean Boussier*

Author: Jacopo Beschi <beschi.jacopo@gmail.com>
Date:   Mon Sep 15 19:51:59 2025 +0200

    Prevent stack overflow in ActionText PlaintextConversion (#55025)
    
    * Prevent stack overflow in ActionText PlaintextConversion
    
    In our app, we encountered edge cases where the ActionText plaintext conversion caused stack overflows.
    To address this, traverse a copy of the tree iteratively bottom-up, converting each node's content
    to plaintext using the already-converted children content. Finally, extract the result from the root node.
    This approach avoids recursion preventing stack overflows.
    
    * Update actiontext/lib/action_text/plain_text_conversion.rb
    
    Co-authored-by: Mike Dalessio <mike.dalessio@gmail.com>
    
    * Update tests for list elements separated by new lines
    
    * Make it non-destructive

def expand_from_hash(attributes, &block)
        return [Arel.sql("1=0", retryable: true)] if attributes.empty?

        attributes.flat_map do |key, value|
          if key.is_a?(Array) && key.size == 1
            key = key.first
            value = value.flatten
          end

          if key.is_a?(Array)
            queries = Array(value).map do |ids_set|
              raise ArgumentError, "Expected corresponding value for #{key} to be an Array" unless ids_set.is_a?(Array)
              expand_from_hash(key.zip(ids_set).to_h)
            end
            grouping_queries(queries)
          elsif value.is_a?(Hash) && !table.has_column?(key)
            table.associated_table(key, &block)
              .predicate_builder.expand_from_hash(value.stringify_keys)
          elsif (associated_reflection = table.associated_with(key))
            # Find the foreign key when using queries such as:
            # Post.where(author: author)
            #
            # For polymorphic relationships, find the foreign key and type:
            # PriceEstimate.where(estimate_of: treasure)

            if associated_reflection.polymorphic?
              value = [value] unless value.is_a?(Array)
              klass = PolymorphicArrayValue
            elsif associated_reflection.through_reflection?
              associated_table = table.associated_table(key)

              next associated_table.predicate_builder.expand_from_hash(
                associated_table.primary_key => value
              )
            end

            klass ||= AssociationQueryValue
            queries = klass.new(associated_reflection, value).queries.map! do |query|
              # If the query produced is identical to attributes don't go any deeper.
              # Prevents stack level too deep errors when association and foreign_key are identical.
              query == attributes ? self[key, value] : expand_from_hash(query)
            end

            grouping_queries(queries)
          elsif table.aggregated_with?(key)
            mapping = table.reflect_on_aggregation(key).mapping
            values = value.nil? ? [nil] : Array.wrap(value)
            if mapping.length == 1 || values.empty?
              column_name, aggr_attr = mapping.first
              values = values.map do |object|
                object.respond_to?(aggr_attr) ? object.public_send(aggr_attr) : object
              end
              self[column_name, values]
            else
              queries = values.map do |object|
                mapping.map do |field_attr, aggregate_attr|
                  self[field_attr, object.try!(aggregate_attr)]
                end
              end

              grouping_queries(queries)
            end
          else
            self[key, value]
          end
        end

def determine_delay(seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm:, executions:, jitter: JITTER_DEFAULT)
        jitter = jitter == JITTER_DEFAULT ? self.class.retry_jitter : (jitter || 0.0)

        case seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm
        when :exponentially_longer
          delay = executions**4
          delay_jitter = determine_jitter_for_delay(delay, jitter)
          delay + delay_jitter + 2
        when ActiveSupport::Duration, Integer
          delay = seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm.to_i
          delay_jitter = determine_jitter_for_delay(delay, jitter)
          delay + delay_jitter
        when Proc
          algorithm = seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm
          algorithm.call(executions)
        else
          raise "Couldn't determine a delay based on #{seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm.inspect}"
        end

content.text:
# Rails upgrade risk report for Margin Notes: 7.0.8.7 to 8.1.0

This upgrade crosses four release series (7.1, 7.2, 8.0, 8.1). Most of what changes for this app is deprecated behavior that 7.1 warned about and 7.2 or 8.0 removed. Skipping straight to 8.1 means you never see those warnings.

I compared the released gems (all 12 Rails components for 7.0.8.7 and 8.1.0, plus `action_text-trix` 2.1.19 and `sidekiq` 6.5.12), the CHANGELOGs for 7.1 through 8.1, and Rails commit history. I didn't install, run or change anything in the app. The unpacked sources are in `/tmp/railsdiff/src/`.

Each claim is tagged with where it comes from:
- **[CL]** a CHANGELOG entry
- **[code]** gem or app source I read
- **[inf]** my own inference

I rated 8 changes high, 4 medium and 15 low. Your test suite would catch most of the high-risk ones, but two can't be caught by tests at all: the BigDecimal job-argument change during a rolling deploy, and the Astana time zone.

## Facts about the app the ratings depend on (please correct any that are wrong)

- **Ruby and Rails:** Ruby 3.3.6. Rails 8.1 needs at least 3.2 [code].
- **Framework defaults:** `config.load_defaults 7.0` (`config/application.rb:12`). Nothing opts into later defaults. All ratings assume you keep 7.0 defaults.
- **Database:** PostgreSQL only, through pg 1.6.0. MySQL, SQLite and Trilogy changes don't apply.
- **Rendering:** the app renders HTML with ERB, Turbo, importmap and Sprockets. There are no JSON endpoints and no Jbuilder views.
- **Background jobs:** Active Job runs on Sidekiq 6.5.12 with redis 4.8.1 (`config/application.rb:24`). Tests use the `:test` adapter.
  - Active Job classes: `CitationEnrichmentJob`, `DigestJob`, `NoteReminderJob`.
  - `ExportJob` is a native Sidekiq job.
  - Reminder jobs can sit in Sidekiq's schedule for weeks.
  - I assumed web servers and workers on different Rails versions can run side by side during a deploy.
- **Rich text and files:** Action Text with a custom tag allowlist and a vendored Trix 1.3.5. Active Storage uses the local Disk service, with no image processor.
- **Caching:** production uses the default cache store with `perform_caching = true`. `app/views/exports/_export.html.erb:26` uses fragment caching. Dev and test use `null_store`.
- **Time zones:** the app zone is UTC, and each reader has a zone in `users.time_zone`.
- **Mail:** sent with `deliver_now` from inside jobs.
- **Configuration:** provider settings come from `config/secrets.yml` via `Rails.application.secrets`.
- **Unused frameworks:** no Action Cable channels or client, and no Action Mailbox.

**Version recommendation:** target 8.1.4 rather than 8.1.0 [CL]. 8.1.0 is missing later security fixes for code this app uses:
- Active Storage Disk service path traversal (CVE-2026-33195) and glob injection (CVE-2026-33202)
- direct-upload metadata filtering (CVE-2026-33173), which Trix uploads go through
- NumberHelper (CVE-2026-33176, CVE-2026-33169) and `SafeBuffer#%` (CVE-2026-33170)

The 7.0 series no longer gets fixes [inf]. I only reviewed up to 8.1.0, not 8.1.1–8.1.4.

## High risk: behavior changes without an error

**1. `return` inside a transaction now commits instead of rolling back**
- **Before:** in 7.0, leaving a transaction block with `return` rolled back any writes [code].
- **Now:** it commits. 7.1 restored committing on early return behind a config setting, and 7.2 made committing the only behavior [CL] ([#48600](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/48600), [eccc606](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/eccc6061f4f3abdfdeb9a363987a898418d9498f)).
- **Where:** `app/models/import.rb:53-58`, which runs `save!` and then `return false unless row.note.save`.
- **What could go wrong:** a CSV with one invalid row would save the `Import` and every note before that row. This breaks the "saves nothing" promise in `ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- **Tests:** `test/controllers/imports_controller_test.rb:65-72` would catch it [inf].

**2. Job time arguments now keep the reader's time zone**
- **Before:** a `TimeWithZone` job argument was rebuilt in `Time.zone`, which is UTC here [code].
- **Now:** it is rebuilt in the zone it was serialized with [CL] ([#50240](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/50240)).
- **Where:**
  - `app/models/user.rb:35,41` passes the request time in the reader's zone.
  - `app/mailers/digest_mailer.rb:8-9` uses `.to_date` and `.all_day` on it.
- **What could go wrong:** digests would cover the reader's local day instead of the UTC day. The Redis reservation key is still the UTC date (`user.rb:36`). Comments in `digest_job.rb:4-5` and `digest_mailer.rb:3-5` become wrong.
- **Tests:** `test/controllers/digests_controller_test.rb:33-35` would fail [inf].

**3. BigDecimal job arguments use a format Rails 7.0 workers can't read**
- **Before:** in 7.0, a BigDecimal was passed through raw and arrived in the worker as a string [code].
- **Now:** it uses `BigDecimalSerializer`, which 7.0 doesn't have. 7.1 added it behind a flag "to avoid deploy races", and 7.2/8.0 removed the flag [CL] ([#45618](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/45618), [2a761d2](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/2a761d23d2322f3cf406aba0426ea356673da508)).
- **Where:** `app/models/user.rb:41` passes `reading_completion`.
- **What could go wrong:** during a rolling deploy, a digest queued by an 8.1 web process and picked up by a 7.0 worker fails to deserialize. Sidekiq would retry it, so delivery is late and noisy rather than lost [inf].
- **Tests:** can't catch this. `BigDecimal(params[:completion])` handles both formats.

**4. `HashWithIndifferentAccess#stringify_keys` now converts integer keys**
- **Before:** integer keys were left as integers.
- **Now:** every key becomes a string [CL] ([#53125](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53125)). 8.1 has no override, so the generic `stringify_keys` applies [code].
- **Where:**
  - `app/models/import.rb:38-42` keys annotations by integer line number.
  - `app/views/imports/preview.html.erb:22` calls `.stringify_keys`, then lines 42-44 look up `annotations[row.line]` with an integer.
- **What could go wrong:** every annotation silently disappears from the import preview.
- **Tests:** `imports_controller_test.rb:22,24` would fail [inf].

**5. `citation[:id]` no longer returns the `doi` primary key**
- **Before:** `read_attribute(:id)` mapped to the custom primary key [code].
- **Now:** `citations` has no `id` column, and 8.1 quietly returns `nil` instead of raising [code] (`activemodel` `AttributeSet::Builder#default_attribute` → `Attribute.null`). This was deprecated in 7.1 and removed in 7.2 [CL] ([#49019](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/49019), [39997a0](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/39997a0f049dfb3d94b28d1cb131b9136a1b7b0a)).
- **Where:** `app/models/import.rb:68`.
- **What could go wrong:** the receipt CSV's `doi` column comes out empty.
- **Tests:** `imports_controller_test.rb:45` would fail.

**6. `TimeWithZone#to_time` now keeps the zone instead of the fixed offset**
- **Before:** `to_time` kept the fixed UTC offset [code].
- **Now:** it always keeps the zone [CL, 8.1] ([c79dc28](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/c79dc282d687cff1c5dc81e19d27257dca5e6a80)).
- **Where:** `app/models/note.rb:43-45` (`reminder_at.to_time + 86_400`), shown in `app/views/notes/_reminder.html.erb:19`.
- **What could go wrong:** across a daylight saving change, the "24 hours later" preview becomes 08:00 -05:00 instead of 09:00 -04:00. I confirmed this with a plain-Ruby stub zone [inf]. The epoch that actually gets scheduled is unchanged [inf].
- **Tests:** `reminders_controller_test.rb:21` would fail.

**7. The "Astana" time zone now maps to UTC+5 instead of UTC+6**
- **Change:** "Astana" changed from `Asia/Dhaka` to `Asia/Almaty` [code, CL] ([#51317](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/51317)). Asia/Almaty is UTC+5 in current tzdata [inf].
- **Where:** readers with that zone, through `app/models/user.rb:13,22`, `note.rb:37` and `accounts/edit.html.erb:15`.
- **What could go wrong:** new local-time reminders shift by an hour, and displayed times change.
- **Tests:** can't catch this. Query production for users with this zone.
- Other mapping changes ("Canberra" and "Greenland" moved to new zone IDs, and "Asuncion" was added) don't change the offset. Only "Astana" matters.

**8. Action Text plain-text conversion changed**
- **Before:** `<script>` and `<style>` text was included, and ordered-list numbers counted whitespace text nodes. For example `<ol>\n<li>` gave "2.", "4." [code].
- **Now:** script and style text is dropped, and numbering is 1, 2 [code] ([#54226](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/54226), [0a5faea](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/0a5faeaf71745b05d937b579a4da5bd90e0b6b58)).
- **Where:** Markdown exports (`app/models/export.rb:78`), and previews in `notes/index.html.erb:53` and `imports/preview.html.erb:58`.
- **What could go wrong:** only bodies imported from CSV are likely to contain such HTML [inf]. These are fixes, but they silently change what export files contain.

## Medium risk: raises an error, and the fix needs a decision

**9. `Rails.application.secrets` was removed**
- **Change:** deprecated in 7.1, removed in 7.2 [CL] ([0c76f17](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/0c76f17f2dbf0d7ad90c890e6f334743cacce41f)).
- **Where:**
  - `app/models/citation/provider.rb:13` and `config/secrets.yml`
  - tests in `test/controllers/citation_enrichments_controller_test.rb:45,117-122`
- **What could go wrong:** the error doesn't appear at boot. It's a `NoMethodError` inside `CitationEnrichmentJob` [inf]. That isn't a `Provider::Error`, so Sidekiq retries it and the citation stays "pending". `ARCHITECTURE.md` also documents this setup.
- **Decision:** move to credentials, `config_for`, or plain ENV. `config_for` also returns symbol keys [inf].

**10. Action Text's `allowed_tags` now defaults to `nil`**
- **Change:** `ActionText::ContentHelper.allowed_tags` defaults to `nil`, and the built-in defaults are computed in `sanitizer_allowed_tags` [code] ([#48746](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/48746)).
- **Where:** `config/initializers/action_text.rb:3` does `allowed_tags += ...`.
- **What could go wrong:** boot fails with `NoMethodError` on `nil`. The obvious fix, setting it to just `%w[details summary]`, would silently strip all other formatting and attachments.
- **Decision:** rebuild the list from the sanitizer defaults plus `action-text-attachment`, `figure`, `figcaption`, `details` and `summary`. If you later adopt the HTML5 sanitizer, recheck the list.

**11. Rails' built-in Sidekiq adapter is deprecated and will be removed in 8.2**
- **Change:** `check_adapter` warns when you set `queue_adapter = :sidekiq` [CL, code] ([#53058](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53058)). Sidekiq 6.5.12 still works with 8.1's adapter; I checked its `configure_client` and `on` APIs [code].
- **Where:** `config/application.rb:24`.
- **Decision:** the replacement is Sidekiq 7.3.3 or later, which switches to the `redis-client` gem. These Sidekiq-side changes are from memory, not verified in this review [inf]:
  - `redis.sadd` returns an Integer, and `0` is truthy in Ruby, so the digest de-duplication in `user.rb:38` silently breaks.
  - `rescue Redis::BaseError` in `notebook.rb:28` and `Redis::CannotConnectError` in the digest test stop matching.
  - Strict arguments reject the symbol-keyed `{ format: "markdown" }` in `notebook.rb:26`.

**12. Trix now comes from the `action_text-trix` gem (Trix 2.1.x)**
- **Change:** Action Text no longer vendors Trix [CL] ([d0d2d31](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/d0d2d31f62cae9bdc9360b9f179b4311377e9957)).
- **Where:**
  - `*= require trix` in `app/assets/stylesheets/actiontext.css:6` would load the Trix 2.1.19 stylesheet [code].
  - `app/views/layouts/application.html.erb:13` still loads the vendored Trix 1.3.5 script.
- **What could go wrong:** nothing raises. The risk is a styling mismatch between the editor and its stylesheet [inf].
- **Decision:** keep the vendored editor, or adopt the gem's Trix 2 and drop the vendored file. Check the editor visually either way.

## Low risk: mechanical changes that booting or running tests would catch

- `note.rb:12`: `serialize :tags, JSON` raises `ArgumentError` at class load. Use `coder: JSON` [code, CL] ([8069cc8](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/8069cc83e8a508e3f578c49be9007b08e3c5516e)).
- `note.rb:10`: `enum status: ..., _prefix: true` raises `ArgumentError`. Use `enum :status, {...}, prefix: true` [code] ([b9226a6](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/b9226a68bb18283f9f80e73c4bfa77f2a5309740)).
- `note.rb:14`: `alias_attribute :highlight_color, :color` raises when the first `Note` is created, because `color` is a store accessor and not an attribute. Replace it with a reader and writer `alias_method` pair [code] ([94d24f4](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/94d24f45047c3f557828e54986e106120e8ca2d6)).
- `notes_controller.rb:12`: `where(notebooks: @notebook)` used to be singularized to the `notebook` association. It now produces SQL against a `notes.notebooks` column that doesn't exist. Use `where(notebook:)` [code] ([4bf2c4c](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/4bf2c4cea19c422bb3358d4c2ddad6db7247604f)).
- `citation_enrichment_job.rb:7`: `wait: :exponentially_longer` raises "Couldn't determine a delay" only when the provider is unavailable, not at boot. `:polynomially_longer` uses the same formula. The test at `citation_enrichments_controller_test.rb:60-71` covers it [code] ([03dae98](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/03dae98092e21260eb588f432af4bc2bd92d096b)).
- `note.rb:61`: `set(wait_until: <Integer>)` raises `NoMethodError` (`Integer#utc`) when the job is serialized. Use `Time.at(epoch)` [code] ([7982896](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/798289699d49c7443ce11b495444cb900d72c59e)).
- `export.rb:42`: `fragments.sum` over strings raises `TypeError`, because Rails' `Enumerable#sum` override was removed. Use `join`. It already prints a deprecation warning under 7.0 [code] ([3ec6297](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/3ec629784cac7a8b518feb402475153465cd8e96)).
- `notes/index.html.erb:12`: `form_with(model: nil, ...)` raises `ArgumentError`. Drop `model: nil` [code] ([0c150ba](https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/0c150bacaaca7772121300ca124e3ed5392f6ab9)).
- `config/routes.rb:18`: `get "/notes", "/journal", to:` raises "Wrong number of arguments". Split it into two routes. ## Not relevant to this app, with reasons

- **Defaults that only change if you raise `load_defaults`.** Each of these would break app code if you opt in [code]:
  - `postgresql_adapter_decode_dates`: `Date.iso8601(Date)` in `notebook.rb:40` would raise.
  - `raise_on_assign_to_attr_readonly`: the notebook form resubmits the read-only slug.
  - `default_column_serializer = nil`: `serialize :preferences` would raise.
  - Others with no breakage found: the HTML5 sanitizer, `strict_freshness` (affects ETag handling on the export download), and `remove_hidden_field_autocomplete`.
- **Enqueueing jobs after the transaction commits.** The 8.1 default is `false`, so jobs still enqueue inside `with_lock` as the code expects [code].
- **YAML column serializer:** still the default, and `preferences` stays readable [code].
- **MySQL, SQLite and Trilogy adapter changes:** the app uses PostgreSQL.
- **Action Cable:** no channels. The Redis adapter still accepts redis 4 [code].
- **Action Mailbox, Solid Queue/Cache/Cable, authentication generator, Kamal, `bin/ci`:** not used.
- **JSON rendering and escaping changes:** the app has no JSON endpoints.
- **Active Storage variants and image analyzers, and S3/GCS/Azure services:** no image processor, and only the Disk service is used.
- **Changes to the cache format, MemCache or Redis cache stores:** cache format 7.0 is still supported, and no Redis or MemCache store is used [code].
- **`ActiveRecord::Base.connection`** in `notebook.rb:40`: only soft-deprecated, with no warning by default [code].
- **`rich_text_area`:** still available as an alias [code].
